name: Bending Points
description: Find all points where the curvature of a curve is locally maximal. I.e. the points where the curve bends more than in directly adjacent portions. This is useful for checking whether curves adhere to curvature limitations, either due to manufacturing or material strength constraints.

name: Curve Curvature
description: Compute the curvature magnitude and direction at a locus along a curve.

name: Curve End Points
description: Get the start and end points of a curve. Every curve in Rhinoceros and Grasshopper has exactly one start and one end point. When the curve is closed, these two points are coincident and they lie at the curve seam.

name: Curve End Tangents
description: Get the start and end tangent vectors of a curve. Every curve in Rhinoceros and Grasshopper has exactly one start and one end tangent.

name: Arc 2 Tangents
description: Create both arcs that satisfy a start and end tangent constraint. The two tangent vectors define the angles the arcs must cover from start to finish. This constraint locks down the shapes, but not the sizes of the arcs.

name: Arch In Rectangle
description: Create a historically common arch shape within a rectangle. The geometric definition of most arch types includes an angle, which controls some crucial aspect of the shape. Note that the angle will mean very different things for different arch types, so an angle which works well for Trefoil arches will yield very awkward results for Horseshoe arches.

name: Circle 2 Points
description: Create a circle out of a base plane and two points. This is analogous to the _2Point option in the Rhinoceros _Circle command.

name: Circle From Value
description: Create a circle based on a numerical value, the contextual meaning of which is picked out of a list of presets.

name: Circle N Points
description: Create a circle which best approximates a collection of points. This is analogous to the Fit Points option in the Rhinoceros _Circle command.

name: Circle Radius
description: Create a circle from a base plane and a radius. This is the most fundamental way to create a circle, as it mirrors the way circles are defined in Rhinoceros.

name: Osculating Circle
description: Compute the osculating circle at a specific location on a curve. An osculating circle shares the location, tangent direction, and curvature of the underlying curve at the specified locus. As such, it can be thought of as a higher order tangent line.

name: Trim Curve at Loci
zhName: 修剪 曲线 在 loci

name: Blend Curve
description: Create a blend curve connecting the end of one guide curve to the start of another. This component offers no control over the blend other than the continuity constraints in input Bc, which are shown in the table below. The resulting blend's bulge factors are hard-coded to 1.

name: Blend Curve Custom
description: Create a smooth blend curve which connects the end of one guide curve to the start of another, using custom bulge factors and continuity.

name: Connect Curves
description: Create blend curves connecting a sequence of guide curves. This component outputs both the fully joined result, as well as the individual connecting blend curves.

name: Curve From Angle
description: Create a planar curve whose tangent angle is determined by a given function at each point along its length. The angle at length l as measured along the curve, equals the value of the function f(l). The function values can be interpreted as either degrees or radians.

name: Curve From Curvature
description: Create a planar curve whose curvature is determined by a given function at each point along its length. The curvature at length l as measured along the curve, equals the value of the function f(l), with positive and negative values bending the curve in opposite directions.

name: Line 2 Points
description: Create a finite line segment connecting two points. This is the most fundamental way to create a line, as it mirrors the way lines are defined in Rhinoceros.

name: Line Cue Points
description: Create a finite line segment between the projections of two points onto a pre-existing infinite line. This is analogous to the FourPoint option in the Rhinoceros _Line command.

name: Line Explicit
description: Create a finite line segment coincident with the hypothetical infinite line described by an equation in the form y=ax+b. In this equation, a encodes the slope of the line, while b encodes the location where the line intercepts the y-axis.

name: Line Implicit
description: Create a finite line segment coincident with the hypothetical infinite line described by an equation in the form ax+by+c=0. The ratio of a and b controls the angle of the line, while the c factor affects the distance between the line and the origin.

name: Line Into Cloud
description: Shoot a line into a point cloud and terminate at the first collision. The radius of each point is sampled from a given scalar field, so in fact the cloud consists of spheres.

name: Line N Points
description: Create the line which best approximates a collection of points. The line fitter algorithm aims to minimise the fitting error of the resulting line. The error is calculated by summing the squares of the distances from each point to the line.

name: Line Span
description: Create a finite line segment based on a starting point and a span vector. The span vector controls both the direction and length of the line.

name: Line Through Sphere
description: Create the finite portion of an infinite line segment which exists on the interior of a sphere.

name: Non-crossing Lines
description: Connect two equally large sets of points with lines so that no two lines intersect. There are often several solutions for any given pair of point sets. Note that it is not possible to select a specific solution with this component, or indeed view multiple solutions.

name: Rectangle Bounding Lines
description: Create lines connecting a point with the two outermost rectangle corners, which are visible from the point location. The point must be outside of the rectangle for this to work.

name: Repeat Items
description: Create a new list by repeating the items in an existing list a fixed number of times. Items are repeated individually, i.e. the first item in the existing list occurs N times in the output list before the second item appears.

name: Assign Display·Colour
description: This component assigns the Display.Colour meta data to values. This will affect the colour of the object when displayed in the Rhinoceros viewports.

name: Elevation Display
description: Colour the vertices of a mesh based on their elevation. The elevations are measured as the signed distance from each vertex to the zero-plane.

name: Visibility Display
description: Determine the visibility of all mesh vertices from a given observer location. The mesh is split into two regions; those portions visible to the observer, and those occluded from view.

name: Adjust HSL
description: Change the Hue, Saturation and Luminance properties of a colour without switching to another colour space.

name: Change Colour Space
description: Translate a colour from its current space to a different one. In Grasshopper 2, colours are defined as coordinates in a predefined set of colour spaces, including sRGB, HSL and L*a*b*.

name: Evaluate Gradient
description: Measure the colour of a gradient at a parameter along its length.

name: Gradient From Interval
description: Create a colour gradient by distributing a provided set of colours within a numeric interval using equal spacing.

name: Gradient Functions
description: Extract the interpolation functions of a colour gradient. Gradients in Grasshopper 2 are defined using a collection of colour grips, a colour space, and an interpolation scheme.

name: Combine Date And Time
zhName: combine 日期 and 时间

name: Random Chords In Rectangle
zhName: 随机 chords in 矩形

name: Random Integers
description: Create a collection of random integers within a particular discrete statistical distribution. Most commonly the distribution is a uniform one, such as [0,100] or [−10,+10], and this can be quickly specified by connecting integer or interval values to the Di input, as the first example shows.

name: Random Points In Box
zhName: 随机 点 in 包围盒

name: Random Points In Sphere
zhName: 随机 点 in 球体

name: Random Points On Box
zhName: 随机 点 on 包围盒

name: Random Points On Sphere
zhName: 随机 点 on 球体

name: Angle Degrees
description: This component constructs an angle from a numeric degree value.

name: Angle In Degrees
description: This component converts angles specified in any angular unit system into angles specified in degrees.

name: Angle Radians
description: This component constructs an angle from a numeric radian value.

name: Angle Slope
description: This component constructs an angle from a slope or grade percentage. Grades and slopes are almost exclusively used in infrastructure to signal the steepness of a particular road.

name: Angle Turns
description: This component constructs an angle from a number of full turns.

name: Mesh Colours From Field
zhName: 网格 颜色 从 field

name: Preset Picker
description: The Preset Picker object shows the preset values of input parameters, if they are available. Some component inputs have predefined, named values which carry special meaning. Most often these are integers which represent an option, but texts, Booleans, and in fact any other parameter type has the ability to define presets.

name: Panel
description: The data panel is the standard way of examining data in Grasshopper. The panel can display both the structure, the types, the values, and the meta data of items.

name: Relay
description: Relays are primarily organisational objects which allow for the rerouting of wires to remove visually awkward bundles, also known as spaghetti.

name: Scratch
description: The Scratch object, alongside the Scribble, is used to annotate files. While a scribble contains text, a scratch contains a single curve.

name: Tube Tangent To Plane
zhName: tube 切线 到 平面

name: Tube Tangent To Planes
zhName: tube 切线 到 平面

name: Cartesian Point
description: Create a point using oriented x, y, and z coordinates. The fourth input of this component is a plane, which can be used to override the standard world XY coordinate system.

name: Cycle Points
description: Cycle a list of point until the point with the specified property is the first one.

name: Cylindrical Point
description: Create a point using cylindrical coordinates. The first three inputs represent the coordinate values, i.e. an angle, a radius, and an elevation, while the fourth input defines the space in which these coordinates live.

name: Distance With Metric
description: Compute the distance between two coordinates using a specific metric. Note that unlike regular Distance, this component operates on n-dimensional points.

name: Point 2 Angles
description: Create a point in a plane based on two angles. This is how geographical triangulation works.

name: Point XYZ
description: Create a point in standard world space from x, y, and z coordinates. This is the most fundamental way to create a point as it mirrors the way 3D points are defined in Rhinoceros.

name: Points Between Planes
description: This component groups points depending on which sides of a set of planes they are positioned. This point-plane-relation is encoded using a textual string, whose characters are either A for above, B for below, or X for invalid.

name: Points To Numbers
description: Convert a list of points into a list of coordinate numbers using a custom pattern.

name: Sort Fuzzy Points
description: Sort points into a collection of columns whose x-coordinates are similar within tolerance. This is most commonly used to reverse-engineer an orthogonal grid of points from a flat, unordered list.

name: Spherical Point
description: Create a point using spherical coordinates. The first three inputs represent the coordinate values, i.e. an xy angle, a z angle, and a radius, while the fourth input defines the space in which these coordinates live.

name: Circles On Disc
description: Place small circles within a large circle based on a given stacking method. The available methods are:
